title: Native kit: a Sheet or Dialog opened while another kit overlay is presented renders inside that overlay's own Modal (one overlay stack, closes resolved before opens), so iOS never gets a second sibling modal
rootCause:
One cause, in the @dos/ui native kit. It is not in any screen, the backend, sync or the worker: the refused tap sends 0 POST (QA/evidence/batch1/regression/ios/manager-020-stuck-after-refused-dialog.txt), so no server path is involved. Checked against RN 0.86.3 / Expo SDK 57 (frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml:42,45).

1. Sheet and Dialog are two separate React Native `<Modal>`s. `Sheet` renders `<Modal visible={open} transparent animationType="slide">` (frontend/libs/ui/src/native/feedback.tsx:139). `Dialog` renders its own `<Modal visible={open} transparent animationType="fade">` (:226). Screens render the Dialog as a SIBLING after the Sheet: manager-app/app/orders/index.tsx has Sheet :496-674 and Dialogs :676 and :731, opened by `setDeciding` from buttons inside the Sheet (:541/:554); money/index.tsx has Sheet :268-360 and Dialogs :469/:504/:538, opened by `setReversing(true)` :352, `setDepositing(true)` :327 and `setBouncing(true)` :340 inside the Sheet. 22 files render both (manager 13, owner 6 including the approvals swap, admin 3). None nests a Dialog in a Sheet's children, and no screen opens a second Sheet from inside a first (manager inbound/index.tsx:347 and billing/credit-notes.tsx:275 open theirs from the page). The field apps (sales, warehouse, delivery, retailer) have Sheets but no Dialog in the same file.

2. iOS presents a Modal from the view controller that owns the host view. `presentViewController` calls `[[self reactViewController] presentViewController:…]` (frontend/node_modules/react-native/React/Fabric/Mounting/ComponentViews/Modal/RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm:150-156), and `reactViewController` walks `nextResponder` to the first UIViewController (React/Views/UIView+React.m:282-292). A sibling Dialog's host view sits in the screen hierarchy, so the walk reaches EXAppViewController and UIKit picks EXRootViewController, which is already presenting the Sheet's RCTFabricModalHostViewController. UIKit refuses; that is exactly the logged line 'Attempt to present <RCTFabricModalHostViewController> on <EXRootViewController> (from <EXAppViewController>) which is already presenting' (manager-020-ios-log-nested-modal.txt, manager-034-bank-it-in-sheet-evidence.txt, manager-034-mark-bounced-in-sheet-evidence.txt). A host view that is a DESCENDANT of an open modal's content lives in that modal controller's view (RCTFabricModalHostViewController.mm:41-47, RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm:312-315), resolves to that controller and presents from it. That is the path RupeeInput's pad `<Modal>` (native/money.tsx:415) takes inside a Sheet (by code; never walked on iOS).

3. Why the dialog stays dead. `ensurePresentedOnlyIfNeeded` sets `_isPresented = YES` before the present call (RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm:165-182) and nothing clears it when UIKit refuses (the completion never runs). Props updates only re-run that check (:300-301), so nothing retries while `visible` stays true. Closing the Sheet therefore never shows the Dialog, and the screen's `open` (`deciding !== null`, orders/index.tsx:732) cannot be cancelled because the Dialog is invisible. The queue-card Approve (:463/:475) only swaps `deciding` for a new object, `open` stays true, and nothing is presented. Only that Dialog instance is stuck; another Dialog on the screen still presents once the Sheet is gone. It recovers only when its host view is recycled (`prepareForRecycle` resets `_isPresented`, :271-278), that is when the screen unmounts or the app relaunches. The finding saw relaunch; a screen remount was not walked.

4. Why web, Android and the owner pass. Web Sheet and Dialog are plain stacked divs (libs/ui/src/web/feedback.tsx:175-326). On Android each RN Modal is its own dialog window, so siblings stack (QA/14 Android rows DOS-020 and DOS-034 PASS). Owner approvals.tsx:266 hides the Sheet while its Dialog shows (`open={current !== null && confirm === null}`; Sheet :265 before Dialog :322), a swap instead of a stack. ios-results.json 'DOS-020-owner' records the FORWARD swap working on iOS 18 ('the Approvals Sheet closes before it opens'). The backward swap (Cancel calls `setConfirm(null)`, which reopens the Sheet in the same commit) was never walked on iOS.

The finding's suggested fix is half right. 'Render the Dialog inside the Sheet's own Modal' is the correct direction. 'Close the Sheet and reopen it' per screen loses the Sheet's children on iOS (Modal.js:278-289 unmounts them once dismissed), flickers, and must be copied into 21 screens. 'Make Dialog re-present after a refusal' is unnecessary once kit overlays never compete; refusals caused by non-kit presenters stay out of scope (risk 4).

changes.what:
Platform-neutral pure-TS store (no react or react-native import, so vitest runs it). `createOverlayStack<T>()` returns: `request(id, open, onClose)` (records an open or close INTENT); `remove(id)` (records an unmount); `flush()` (applies the intents, then emits once); `roleOf(id): 'root' | 'layer' | null`; `hostOf(id)`; `isPresented(rootId)`; `hasLayers(rootId)`; `setLayer(id, render: T | null)`; `layersOf(rootId)` (open order, an array whose identity changes only when that host's version changes); `version(rootId)`; `requestClose(rootId)`; `subscribe(listener)`; `presentedRoots()`.

Rules, applied inside `flush()`:
(1) Removes and closes first, then opens, each in request order. The result never depends on which overlay is earlier in the React tree. (Layout effects run in tree order, and owner approvals.tsx renders its Sheet :265 before its Dialog :322.)
(2) An overlay opened while a root is presented (open, or retained by open layers) becomes a LAYER of that root. Otherwise it becomes a ROOT, which owns the one native Modal.
(3) A retained root that is opened again takes its panel back and stays the root. It is never layered into itself.
(4) The role is fixed until the overlay closes, except under rule 6.
(5) A root closed while it has open layers is RETAINED: its Modal stays visible and its panel is gone, until the last layer closes; then it is removed. A root closed with no layers is removed at once.
(6) A layer whose host is REMOVED (unmounted) while the layer is still open is promoted: the oldest such layer becomes the root and the rest become its layers. An open overlay is never left without a host.
(7) `requestClose` calls the top layer's onClose, or the root's own when it has no layers.
(8) Invariant after every flush: `presentedRoots().length <= 1`.
`setLayer` bumps only its host's version and emits; it never changes a role.

Red-first order (the DOS-146 plan's pattern): land the module first with TODAY's rule, where every opened overlay is its own root (what feedback.tsx:139/:226 do). Run overlay-stack.test.ts and watch the layering tests fail on assertions. Then implement the rules.

React Native glue for the store. Internal: not exported from native/index.ts, so parity.test.ts is unchanged.
- `OverlayStackContext` and `OverlayStackProvider`. The provider creates the stack once with `useState(() => createOverlayStack<ReactNode>())` and schedules at most one `queueMicrotask(() => stack.flush())` per tick when an intent arrives (RN installs queueMicrotask: Libraries/Core/setUpTimers.js:23-33).
- `useOverlay(open, onClose)`: the id comes from `useId()`; `onClose` is kept in a ref; `role`, `presented` and `hasLayers` are read through `useSyncExternalStore` with PRIMITIVE snapshots, so there are no render loops. A `useLayoutEffect` on `[open]` calls `stack.request(id, open, …)`; unmount calls `stack.remove(id)`. With no provider it returns role 'root', `presented = open`, `hasLayers = false` and `requestClose = onClose`, which is today's behaviour.
- `useLayerContent(overlay, element)`: a layout effect with no dependency array. It calls `stack.setLayer(id, element)` when `stack.roleOf(id)` (read live, not from the render snapshot) is 'layer', and `setLayer(id, null)` otherwise.
- `OverlayOutlet`: `React.memo`, props `{ hostId }`. It re-renders only from the store (`version(hostId)`), never from its parent. A controlled TextInput in a layered Dialog therefore receives each value once, never a stale value that would move the caret. It renders each layer in `<View key={id} style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} accessibilityViewIsModal>` after the host panel.
- `accessibilityViewIsModal` hides only SIBLING views from VoiceOver, so the covered host panel must also be hidden by the `covered` flag in feedback.tsx. Both are required.

Lines 136-278 only; ConnectionStrip, Toast and the 6.13 components are untouched.
- Extract the current Sheet body (the backdrop Pressable and panel, :140-206) into an internal `SheetPanel`, and the current Dialog body (the backdrop View and card, :227-275) into an internal `DialogPanel`. Both are unchanged except for a `covered` flag that sets `accessibilityElementsHidden` and `importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants'` while a layer sits above.
- `Sheet`: `const o = useOverlay(open, onClose)`; `useLayerContent(o, open ? <SheetPanel …/> : null)`. If `o.role === 'layer'`, return `<></>`. Otherwise return `<Modal visible={o.role === 'root' && o.presented} transparent animationType="slide" onRequestClose={o.requestClose}>{open ? <SheetPanel covered={o.hasLayers} …/> : null}<OverlayOutlet hostId={o.id} /></Modal>`.
- `Dialog`: the same with `DialogPanel` and `animationType="fade"`.
- A root's `<Modal>` element stays mounted with `visible={false}` after it closes, so the iOS dismissal animation is kept. It unmounts only while the overlay is a layer, which is a native no-op because a layer's Modal was never presented. The render between `open` flipping and the microtask flush has no role yet and keeps `visible` false for that commit.
- `SheetProps` and `DialogProps` in src/types.ts do not change, no screen changes, and web/feedback.tsx does not change.

Lines 29-35: put `<OverlayStackProvider>` inside `ThemeContextProvider`, around the ground View. Every app root layout mounts the native ThemeProvider in each of its branches (for example manager-app/app/_layout.tsx:74, :176, :187, :194 and admin-app/app/_layout.tsx:57, :152, :164, :171), so no app `_layout.tsx` changes. This follows the file's own reasoning for SafeAreaProvider living there.

Vitest spec for the store holding the DOS-164 store tests listed under tests. Each test records intents, calls `flush()` explicitly, and asserts roles, `presentedRoots()`, layer order, retention, promotion, and which onClose `requestClose` calls. RED on assertions against the today's-rule stub (see overlay-stack.ts), GREEN after.

Source-reading guard in the style of parity.test.ts:200-232 (native files cannot be imported in Node; reuse the `bodyOf` slicing idea from :206-211). It reads native/feedback.tsx and native/ThemeProvider.tsx and asserts four things: no `<Modal visible={open}` remains; the `Sheet` body calls `useOverlay(` and renders `<OverlayOutlet`; the `Dialog` body does the same; ThemeProvider.tsx renders `<OverlayStackProvider>`. RED on the pre-fix main (feedback.tsx:139 and :226 bind `visible={open}`, and ThemeProvider.tsx has no provider), GREEN after. It stops a later edit to the same Sheet body (DOS-152, DOS-159) from bringing back a raw sibling Modal.

§6.12: one paragraph. On a phone, a Sheet or Dialog opened while another is up renders inside that one's modal, because iOS presents one modal at a time. Screens keep rendering them as siblings and never nest or swap them by hand. An overlay's body must not read route-scoped context (D8 a).
Per D6 (a): one row. Native Sheets and Dialogs share one modal per presentation through the @dos/ui overlay stack (DOS-164). UX-00 §6.12 and UX-03 D8's @gorhom/bottom-sheet stays unadopted.

Appium/XCUITest device check with the exit codes of e2e/dos-034-day-end.mjs: 0 = pass, 1 = the FAILs are listed, 2 = a precondition is missing.

It does NOT import QA/tools/ios-drive.mjs or ios-login.mjs. Both are CLIs with top-level await that act on process.argv when loaded (ios-drive.mjs:44-46 and its switch at the end; ios-login.mjs:3-6). It spawns them with execFileSync instead: `node ios-login.mjs <metroPort> <user> <app>`, and `node ios-drive.mjs labels|tap|tapc|has|swipe|type`, which share one WebDriver session through ~/.dos-qa-logs/ios-session.

Preconditions (exit 2):
- Appium :4723 answers /status.
- `xcrun simctl list devices booted` lists a device.
- The manager Metro (`MANAGER_METRO`, default 5174) and the owner Metro (`OWNER_METRO`, default 5173) answer.
- psql reaches `DATABASE_URL`.
- Each SQL pick below returns a row.

Picks by SQL (tenant slug tarsun):
- An order with a pending approval whose order_no is unique.
- An office cash receipt with `mode='cash' and status='collected' and trip_id is null`.
- A cheque receipt with `mode='cheque' and status in ('collected','deposited')`.
Receipts are picked by id, because receipt numbers repeat (DOS-032).

Each UIKit check runs `xcrun simctl spawn booted log show --start '<time of the tap>' --predicate 'process == "Expo Go" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "Attempt to present"'`.

Checks:
(a) As vikas.kadam: Orders, the picked order, then Approve inside the panel. 'Note for the person who asked' appears within 5 s, and no 'Attempt to present' is logged since the tap.
(b) Cancel leaves the panel up (its title is still there). Approve opens the dialog again.
(c) Type a 20+ character note and read it back: the field holds the whole text, in order.
(d) Cancel, then Close. The page-level card Approve opens the dialog.
(e) As meena.joshi: Money, Receipts, the cash receipt, Bank it. 'Bank slip number' appears and no refusal is logged.
(f) The cheque receipt, Mark bounced: 'Cheque returned' appears. Tap 'Bank charges': the number pad ('Done') opens on top, a native Modal presented from a layer. Done, then Cancel.
(g) Control on an unchanged path: Money, Receipts, 'Record a payment'. The 'Money from a shop' panel's amount field opens the pad from a ROOT Sheet (money/index.tsx:419).
(h) Owner swap in both directions: as sunil.tarsun on the owner Metro, Approvals, a row, Approve: the confirm dialog opens. Cancel: the approval panel is back. Approve: the dialog opens again. No refusal is logged across the three presentations.

Read-only by default. `--write` refuses a DATABASE_URL ending in /dos_qa. On a copy it approves the picked order's gate from (b), banks the cash receipt from (e) with slip DEP-164, and asserts the approvals and receipts rows.

On the pre-fix main Metros it is RED, with FAIL on (a)-(f). (g) and (h) are controls expected to pass on both builds. If (h)'s backward swap fails before the fix, record it as a separate finding and bring D7 back to the architect. GREEN after the fix.

decisionsNeeded:
This is a shared-kit architecture change used by all seven apps. The architect decides:

D1: where the single native modal lives.
(a) RECOMMENDED. The first presented kit overlay (Sheet or Dialog) is the host. Anything opened while it is up renders as a layer inside that host's Modal. The store lives in the native ThemeProvider. No new export, no app or screen change. A layer renders at its host's place in the tree, which is the same `<Screen>` for all 22 files.
(b) One root host in the native ThemeProvider (or AppShell) that ALWAYS renders every Sheet and Dialog as layers of one Modal. Uniform for any stacking order, but every overlay's children leave their screen's context, slide and fade must be rebuilt in JS, and every Sheet and Dialog in seven apps changes behaviour.
(c) A kit presentation queue: hide the Sheet, wait for onDismiss, show the Dialog, then re-present the Sheet. Nothing is relocated, but the Sheet's children unmount on iOS (Modal.js:278-289), losing scroll and local state, and the panel slides out and back.
(d) A per-screen swap like owner approvals.tsx:266 in the other 21 files. No kit change, but the bug returns with every new in-Sheet dialog, with the same unmount and flicker.
(e) Adopt UX-03 D8 / UX-00 §6.12: `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` v5 `BottomSheetModal` with its portal provider for the Sheet, and a Dialog on the same portal. This means new dependencies (@gorhom/bottom-sheet and @gorhom/portal; reanimated and worklets are only transitive in frontend/node_modules today), a gesture and animation rewrite across seven apps, and the Dialog still needs a host. Too large for this P1; it can follow.
Rejected:
(f) An iOS Dialog through react-native-screens `FullWindowOverlay` (a separate UIWindow, no presentation). It is not a kit peer dependency, a RupeeInput pad `<Modal>` inside it would have no presenting view controller to walk to (unverified), and keyboard and VoiceOver behaviour are unproven.
(g) A native change to present from the top-most controller, because Expo Go allows no custom native code.
(h) `ReactFabric.createPortal`, because it is not a public react-native API.

D2: platforms.
(a) RECOMMENDED: layer on iOS and Android, so there is one native path and the Android walk proves the same code.
(b) iOS only, behind `Platform.OS === 'ios'`. Android keeps sibling dialog windows: less Android change and closer to 'exactly the finding', but two native behaviours, and the Android walk no longer proves the iOS path.

D3: the host closes while its layer is still open (for example a confirm handler clears the Sheet first).
(a) RECOMMENDED: keep the host Modal presented, with its panel removed, until the layer closes. No second presentation and no race.
(b) Close the layer with it. A DOS-029 refusal sentence in that dialog would vanish.
(c) Move the layer to its own Modal after onDismiss. There is a visible gap, and it depends on the iOS-only onDismiss.

D4: layer motion.
(a) RECOMMENDED for this fix: none. A layer appears and leaves instantly over its host.
(b) An Animated fade for a Dialog layer and a slide for a Sheet layer (UX-00 surface motion, 250-300 ms), as a follow-up.

D5: test harness.
(a) RECOMMENDED: a pure store spec and a source-reading guard in vitest (the parity.test.ts pattern), plus the Appium iOS e2e script. No new dependencies.
(b) Add a React Native render harness to @dos/ui (jest-expo or @testing-library/react-native; none is installed in frontend/node_modules today). That means new catalog entries and a second test runner in the frontend workspace.

D6: record the rule.
(a) RECOMMENDED: frontend/libs/ui/README.md §6.12, plus a docs/15-decisions-log.md row that also says UX-03 D8's @gorhom/bottom-sheet stays unadopted.
(b) README only.

D7: a close and an open in the same commit (the owner approvals swap: forward on Approve, backward on Cancel).
(a) RECOMMENDED: closes resolve before opens, so each overlay keeps its own Modal exactly as today, whatever the tree order. This relies on UIKit accepting a presentation while the other modal's dismissal animates: proven forward on iOS 18 (DOS-020-owner), and walked backward in verify step 5.
(b) Layer on coincidence: the closing root is retained and hosts the opening overlay. There is never a second presentation, so no UIKit race at all. But there is no slide or fade, and the owner's Sheet would live inside the Dialog's retained fade Modal until it closes.
(c) Resolve in tree order (the plan as first written). The forward swap gives two Modals and the backward swap layers, so behaviour differs per screen with JSX order.

D8: an overlay opened while an overlay of a DIFFERENT scope is presented: a screen Sheet or Dialog while the shell's More, tenant switcher or rail account sheet is up (native/shell.tsx:70, :309, :432), for example through an async or deep-link open.
(a) RECOMMENDED for this fix: layer it anyway, and record in README §6.12 that an overlay body must not read route-scoped context. `useLocalSearchParams` reads expo-router's LocalRouteParamsContext and would silently return {} there; `useRouter` returns the global router. No overlay body calls either today.
(b) Scope by the kit's `<Screen>`: an open from another scope waits (no role, Modal hidden) until that scope's root closes, then becomes a root. It never gets the wrong context, but it needs more store code and a wait the user can perceive.
(c) The kit closes the shell overlay when a screen overlay opens.

tests.name: DOS-164: a Dialog opened while a Sheet is presented is layered into that Sheet, never a second native modal
DOS-164: the Sheet's modal stays presented while its layered Dialog is open, even after the Sheet itself is closed
DOS-164: a Dialog cancelled over a Sheet and opened again is layered again, so no dialog is left open but unseen
DOS-164: a Dialog opened with nothing presented owns its own modal
DOS-164: a close and an open in the same flush resolve the close first whichever was requested first, so the owner's Sheet/Dialog swap keeps two separate modals in both directions
DOS-164: a retained Sheet opened again takes its panel back and is never layered into itself
DOS-164: a layer whose host unmounts while it is open becomes the root, so it is never left open without a modal
DOS-164: at most one overlay owns a native modal after every flush, for every open/close/unmount order of two Sheets and two Dialogs
DOS-164: onRequestClose (Android back) closes the top layer before its host
DOS-164: native Sheet and Dialog present through the overlay stack, never a Modal bound to their own open prop, and the native ThemeProvider mounts the stack

risk:
Wide blast radius, small visible change. Every native Sheet and Dialog in all seven apps goes through the store, but nothing a user sees changes until two kit overlays are up at once. With one overlay the path is today's single Modal plus one microtask and one extra synchronous commit on open.

(1) Scope. A layer renders at its host's place in the tree. All 22 Sheet+Dialog files render both under the same `<Screen>`, so a layer sees the same context. A screen overlay that opens while a SHELL overlay is up (More, tenant switcher, rail account sheet: native/shell.tsx:70, :309, :432) would render inside the shell's Modal with only AppShell-level context. There, expo-router's `useLocalSearchParams` would silently return {} (it reads LocalRouteParamsContext), while `useRouter` returns the global router. No overlay body calls route hooks today; screens call them at their top (for example manager orders/index.tsx:85). Same-commit navigation from the More sheet is safe because closes resolve before opens (store rule 1). See D8.
(2) A controlled TextInput in a layer depends on OverlayOutlet being memoized and updated only from the store. The verify types into the decision note and the bounce reason on iOS and Android.

WHAT I CHANGED
1. Role resolution is batched. Layout effects record intents, one microtask flushes them, and closes and removes resolve before opens. The original plan resolved roles inside each layout effect, so the result depended on tree order. Owner approvals.tsx renders its Sheet (:265) before its Dialog (:322), so on the backward swap (Cancel → `setConfirm(null)` reopens the Sheet in the same commit) the Sheet's effect would run while the Dialog was still the presented root. The owner's Sheet would then be layered inside the retained fade Dialog, which contradicts the plan's 'the store keeps that path identical'.
2. Two store rules added. A retained root that is opened again takes its panel back; as first written, rule 1 would layer it into itself. A layer whose host unmounts is promoted to root; otherwise it would be exactly this finding's open-but-unseen dialog.
